# Asset Experience and Layered Customization Implementation Roadmap

- Status: `implementation-complete-qualification-pending`
- Updated: `2026-07-18T21:14:33Z`

## Objective

Deliver a responsive card-and-modal Asset Browser, consistent attached tab surfaces for Assets and Systems, a guided Import Assets template experience, and a production-ready workspace-owned layered customization workflow that preserves immutable source assets while exposing authorized definition and implementation internals.

## Discovery

The Asset Browser currently uses fixed-width filters and a two-column list/detail layout; Assets and Systems hand-roll floating tabs while Data Management already uses an attached tabbed panel. Shared modal styling exists without a reusable behavioral component. Package import has a bounded non-executing .aisb-package contract but no starter download. Existing authoring supports safe sparse overrides, while authorized source editing is separately owned by Asset Studio; an integrated derived customization therefore requires an explicit successor decision and coordinated contract, application, host, transport, UI, security, and documentation work.

### Constraints

- Preserve desktop and thin-client feature parity for shared Assets and Systems behavior.
- Reuse shared renderer tokens, modal styling, WorkflowSequence, and the Data Management tabbed-panel presentation.
- Keep source assets, trusted implementation releases, and system.foundation immutable.
- Require explicit workspace identity and exact base definition and implementation references.
- Keep semantic override data separate from bounded authorized source text and implementation artifacts.
- Package browsing and template inspection must remain bounded and non-executing.
- Do not imply public marketplace, automatic update, activation, or unqualified execution support.
- Add regression tests at owning layers and run repository documentation, architecture, agent-support, test, and affected build gates.

### Sources

- [Agent Guide](<../AGENTS.md>) - Defines discovery, decision, impact, verification, and documentation requirements.
- [Documentation Guide](<README.md>) - Routes canonical architecture and roadmap documentation.
- [Asset authoring architecture](<architecture/asset-authoring-customization-and-overrides.md>) - Requires workspace ownership, immutable sources, sparse safe edits, and separate authorized Asset Studio source handling.
- [Asset implementation and package architecture](<architecture/asset-implementations-and-packages.md>) - Separates semantic definitions, implementation releases, package inspection, admission, installation, and activation.
- [WAI modal dialog pattern](<https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/dialog-modal/>) - Requires contained focus, Escape close, accessible naming, and focus restoration.
- [WAI tabs pattern](<https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/tabs/>) - Defines the tab, tablist, and attached tabpanel relationship and keyboard behavior.
- [WCAG 2.2 reflow guidance](<https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/reflow.html>) - Requires non-excepted controls and content to remain usable without two-dimensional page scrolling at narrow equivalent widths.

## High-level decisions

### Customization persistence and source reuse

How should an integrated definition-and-code customization preserve source immutability while creating a modified workspace-owned asset?

The accepted authoring ADR permits sparse semantic overrides but defers raw code there; Asset Studio separately owns bounded authorized source proposals and immutable snapshots. The selected model changes contracts, persistence, provenance, materialization, and conflict handling.

- Status: `approved`
- Selected option: `layered-derived`

| Option | Summary | Recommended | Tradeoffs | Consequences |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Layered derived customization (layered-derived) | Pin a workspace-owned customization to exact base definition and implementation identities, persist sparse semantic changes plus a bounded changed-file overlay, and materialize a complete immutable snapshot only for review, build, and release. | yes | Preserves provenance and avoids logical duplication of unchanged content; Requires a successor ADR and coordinated application workflow | The original asset and release remain immutable; Semantic patches and source overlays remain separate typed records; Conflict detection is based on exact pinned base identities |
| Fully detached copy (detached-copy) | Duplicate the full definition and implementation source into a new workspace draft before editing. | no | Simpler mental model; Duplicates unchanged data and weakens update/conflict semantics | Every customization owns a complete independent source tree; Upstream lineage remains informational rather than structurally reusable |
| Safe fields with separate Studio (safe-fields-only) | Enable searchable safe semantic overrides and retain Asset Studio as a separate code-authoring task. | no | Smallest architecture change; Does not deliver one integrated internals workflow | Current override contracts remain mostly unchanged; Users switch surfaces to customize implementation code |

## Increment 1: Layered customization architecture and contracts

- Id: `architecture-contract`
- Status: `completed`
- Dependencies: None

Ratify the approved layered-derived model and establish stable typed semantics before application or UI consumers are added.

### Work packages

- **Successor architecture decision** (`successor-decision`): An accepted successor ADR defines exact base pinning, workspace ownership, immutable source behavior, sparse semantic patches, bounded source overlays, materialization, conflict handling, and protected fields.
- **Derived customization contract model** (`contract-model`): The asset-authoring contract family represents draft, review, publication, provenance, exact base references, changed semantic fields, changed source files, and safe diagnostics without mixing source bytes into Asset Kernel metadata.
- **Security and contract invariants** (`security-invariants`): Path, size, secret-like content, identity, workspace, immutability, and cross-family boundary invariants are documented and tested.

### Deliverables

- Successor ADR and updated canonical authoring/security architecture
- Additive asset-authoring customization contracts and normalizers
- Contract and anti-drift unit tests
- Updated context packs and status documentation

### Acceptance criteria

| Criterion | Qualification | Latest evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `decision-recorded`: Canonical documentation explicitly distinguishes semantic patches, authorized source overlays, immutable base releases, and materialized derived snapshots. | local | passed (documentation) |
| `contracts-validated`: Typed contracts reject unsafe paths/content, missing workspace or exact base identity, and attempts to mutate protected source identity while accepting bounded sparse changes. | local | passed (test) |
| `docs-pass`: Documentation and architecture checks pass for the approved decision and contract boundary. | local | passed (documentation) |

### Verification

- Run focused asset-authoring contract and architecture invariant tests.
- Run npm run docs:check and npm run architecture:check.

### Rollback

Remove the additive unconsumed contract types and successor documentation before later increments depend on them.

### Excluded

- Persistence and transport implementation
- User-facing customization workflow
- Execution or activation of customized code

## Increment 3: Complete responsive Assets browsing and import experience

- Id: `complete-assets-experience`
- Status: `completed`
- Dependencies: `shared-surface-foundation`

Deliver the complete user-facing Assets browse and import experience across desktop and thin client: responsive asset cards, modal details, responsive filters, Import Assets language, and a safe downloadable .aisb-package starter with complete guidance.

### Work packages

- **Definition and resource card grids** (`card-grid`): Definition and resource-backed results render as responsive, keyboard-operable cards with concise metadata and clear detail actions.
- **Asynchronous detail modal** (`detail-modal`): Selecting a card opens the shared loading-aware detail modal, closes cleanly, restores focus, supports stacked mutation confirmation, and never leaves stale selection.
- **Responsive browse controls** (`responsive-filters`): Search, filters, refresh, and cards use auto-fitting grids that reflow to one column without page-level horizontal overflow.
- **Import Assets language** (`import-language`): Labels, headings, descriptions, accessible names, tests, and documentation consistently say Import Assets while stable internal operation identities remain unchanged.
- **Downloadable package starter** (`starter-template`): A deterministic .aisb-package starter is generated from canonical contract-owned data, contains safe placeholders and example structure, and cannot execute during download or inspection.
- **In-product and canonical authoring guidance** (`import-instructions`): Users can follow manifest, entries, digest, SBOM, provenance, capability, compatibility, inspection, admission, and trust guidance without inferring marketplace or automatic activation support.

### Deliverables

- Desktop and thin-client responsive card-grid Asset Browser
- Shared-modal definition and resource detail experience
- Responsive browse filter and card styling
- Import Assets tab and workflow copy
- Deterministic downloadable .aisb-package starter
- In-product and canonical package-authoring instructions
- Cross-surface component, hook, contract, template, accessibility, and regression tests

### Acceptance criteria

| Criterion | Qualification | Latest evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `card-modal-flow`: Keyboard and pointer activation of either asset-card kind opens the correct loading, success, unavailable, or error detail state in a modal and returns focus on close. | local | passed (test) |
| `responsive-layout`: Cards and filters reduce to usable single-column layouts at narrow widths without clipping controls or creating page-level horizontal scrolling. | local | passed (test) |
| `cross-surface-parity`: Desktop and thin-client tests cover equivalent browse, filter, selection, modal, nested-confirmation, import guidance, and starter-download behavior. | local | passed (test) |
| `template-contract-valid`: The downloaded starter is deterministic, bounded, and validated by the same package contract and inspection rules used for imports, with placeholders clearly identified where user replacement is required. | local | passed (test) |
| `template-non-executing`: Tests prove generation and inspection perform no installation, scripts, activation, network access, or execution. | local | passed (test) |
| `guidance-complete`: The Import Assets page explains the complete safe authoring and import sequence and exposes a working download control on both surfaces. | local | passed (test) |

### Verification

- Run shared Asset Library model and hook tests, both renderer feature suites, package contract and inspection tests, starter-template tests, and presenter tests while implementing internal chunks.
- Near increment completion, run affected desktop and thin-client type/build checks, documentation checks, architecture checks, and the applicable regression suite once.

### Rollback

Retain existing detail presenters as modal bodies so the grid can be reverted independently, and remove additive starter download and guidance without changing Asset Library data semantics or existing package inspection and installation operations.

## Increment 4: End-to-end layered Asset Customization workflow

- Id: `layered-customization-workflow`
- Status: `completed`
- Dependencies: `architecture-contract`, `shared-surface-foundation`, `complete-assets-experience`

Deliver one production-complete vertical slice for searchable exact target selection, sparse layered customization, bounded source overlays, immutable review materialization, workspace-owned publication, and the ordered desktop and thin-client workflow without mutating any base asset.

### Work packages

- **Workspace-scoped customization target catalog** (`target-catalog`): Application-owned list, search, and detail operations expose exact semantic and implementation identities, source kind, eligibility, provenance, editable sections, protected fields, and safe diagnostics for built-in, admitted imported, and authored assets.
- **Source adapters and aligned read transports** (`source-boundaries`): Host-composed readers and API, IPC, preload, and renderer clients map current registries, installed packages, and workspace records into one typed isolated catalog without UI-to-storage access or raw data leakage.
- **Derived customization draft lifecycle** (`draft-lifecycle`): Application use cases own create, read, update, validate, review, publish, and abandon transitions with optimistic revisions and exact pinned bases.
- **Sparse semantic and source-overlay persistence** (`overlay-storage`): Structured records retain semantic patches and safe manifest metadata while content-addressed artifacts retain only bounded changed source files and immutable review snapshots.
- **Asset Studio review materialization** (`studio-materialization`): Authorized boundaries assemble changed and unchanged content into a complete reviewable immutable snapshot; publication creates a new workspace-owned definition and implementation lineage and never activates it.
- **Persistence, host, transport, and client mutation wiring** (`mutation-boundaries`): Desktop and server hosts expose aligned customization operations with authorization, workspace isolation, sanitized diagnostics, optimistic conflict handling, and recoverable failures.
- **Search and select exact base asset** (`select-section`): The first ordered workflow section searches eligible assets, shows source, version, trust, and eligibility, and requires explicit exact selection before editing.
- **Definition, interfaces, and configuration sections** (`definition-sections`): Ordered sections show original and proposed identity, provenance, description, classification, tags, safe metadata, interfaces, schemas, configuration, capabilities, and protected read-only fields.
- **Implementation and source section** (`implementation-section`): Authorized users inspect facets, entry points, dependencies, capabilities, and bounded source files, then add or edit only changed overlay files with clear security diagnostics.
- **Review and create derived asset** (`review-create-section`): A final diff, provenance, and security review identifies reused versus changed content and creates the distinct customization only after explicit confirmation.
- **Customization history and management** (`customization-history`): Existing drafts and published customizations remain searchable with truthful status, conflicts, provenance, and supported disable or abandon actions.

### Deliverables

- Customization target contracts, application read service, and host-composed source readers
- Derived customization application use cases and ports
- Structured and content-addressed artifact persistence adapters
- Asset Studio source-overlay materialization and immutable review integration
- Aligned API, IPC, preload, host, and renderer clients
- Shared ordered WorkflowSequence customization presenter
- Desktop and thin-client Customizations tab integration
- Search, selection, semantic editing, source overlay, review, creation, history, and recovery states
- Lifecycle, immutability, isolation, conflict, transport, accessibility, validation, and negative tests

### Acceptance criteria

| Criterion | Qualification | Latest evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `eligible-sources-searchable`: A workspace can search and select exact eligible built-in or system, admitted installed imported, and authored asset versions with truthful unavailable reasons for unsupported targets. | local | passed (test) |
| `workspace-isolated`: Missing workspace context and cross-workspace imported or authored target reads and writes fail closed while system-owned metadata remains read-only and safely visible. | local | passed (test) |
| `transport-aligned`: API, IPC, preload, host, and client tests prove aligned request, response, error, and operation identities without raw storage or provider data leakage. | local | passed (test) |
| `base-remains-immutable`: Creating, editing, publishing, failing, or abandoning a customization never changes the selected base definition, implementation release, package, authored record, or system-owned source. | local | passed (test) |
| `sparse-reuse`: Unchanged semantic fields and source files remain referenced by exact base identity while only modified fields and files create new customization entries before materialization. | local | passed (test) |
| `safe-materialization`: Review materialization validates containment, sizes, allowed extensions, dependencies, capabilities, secret-like content, digests, and optimistic revisions before producing an immutable snapshot. | local | passed (test) |
| `new-owned-lineage`: Publishing produces a distinct workspace-owned asset lineage with explicit provenance and no implicit build, release, installation, activation, deployment, or execution. | local | passed (test) |
| `selection-controlled`: No customization fields are editable until a specific eligible exact asset version is selected, and changing the target requires explicit confirmation that clears incompatible work. | local | passed (test) |
| `internals-visible`: The workflow shows all important authorized semantic and implementation internals, distinguishes editable, protected, reused, and changed content, and explains why protected fields cannot be edited. | local | passed (test) |
| `ordered-workflow`: Users complete selection, definition, interfaces and configuration, implementation, and review and create sections in a predictable ordered interface consistent with other workflow features. | local | passed (test) |
| `copy-confirmed`: Successful completion visibly creates a new workspace-owned asset and leaves the base unchanged; errors preserve recoverable draft work and expose safe remediation. | local | passed (test) |

### Verification

- Run focused contract, target-reader, application, persistence, artifact-storage, Asset Studio, host, API, IPC, preload, client, workflow, and renderer tests as their internal chunks land.
- Near increment completion, run keyboard-focused UI tests, architecture checks, server and thin-client builds, desktop type and package checks, documentation checks, and the applicable regression suite once.

### Rollback

Keep all new operations additive and capability-gated, retain the existing list and disable view until the guided workflow passes integration, and disable creation without deleting drafts or changing existing authored, package, or base-asset data.

### Excluded

- Reading unadmitted or quarantined package source as an editable asset
- Uncontrolled arbitrary JSON editing
- Direct mutation of imported, built-in, system-owned, or authored base records
- Automatic conflict rebase
- Automatic build, release, installation, activation, deployment, or execution

## Increment 5: Unified resource-backed Asset Studio and Saved assets

- Id: `unified-asset-studio-saved`
- Status: `completed`
- Dependencies: `layered-customization-workflow`

Deliver one ordered Studio surface for creating, saving, reopening, reviewing, and publishing from-scratch semantic assets with actual frontend structure, frontend styling, backend logic, and other backing resources across desktop and thin-client hosts.

### Work packages

- **Workspace-owned resource-backed Studio drafts** (`studio-draft-domain`): A backward-compatible authored-draft evolution coordinates full semantic definition data, exact intended identity, immutable backing-resource artifacts, implementation draft identity, optimistic revision, and lifecycle without storing source text in structured records.
- **Save, reopen, review, and publish lifecycle** (`studio-lifecycle`): Application use cases create, read, list, update, review-materialize, publish, and abandon exact workspace drafts while preserving non-execution, safe diagnostics, and distinct publication and activation gates.
- **Aligned desktop and server boundaries** (`studio-transports`): API, IPC, preload, host composition, and both renderer clients expose the same workspace-isolated Studio draft operations and bounded resource details.
- **One reusable ordered authoring surface** (`shared-studio-sections`): Studio reuses shared semantic and backing-resource section components from Customizations for definition, configuration/interfaces, AI context/composition, frontend structure, frontend styling, backend logic, other resources, and save/review/publish.
- **Saved assets and tab consolidation** (`saved-navigation`): Create is removed; Drafts becomes Saved, lists unpublished workspace assets, and opens an exact draft in the single Studio tab in both hosts.

### Deliverables

- Resource-backed Studio draft contracts, persistence, application lifecycle, and artifact integration
- Aligned API, IPC, preload, host, and client operations
- Shared ordered semantic and backing-resource Studio sections
- Saved-assets list with exact Studio reopening
- Removed Create tab and renamed Drafts tab
- Focused cross-host, workspace-isolation, restart, security, accessibility, and navigation tests
- Updated ADR or architecture guidance, READMEs, context pack, and temporary report

### Acceptance criteria

| Criterion | Qualification | Latest evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `single-studio-surface`: Desktop and thin client each expose one ordered Studio tab that edits both complete semantic definition sections and actual categorized backing resources for a new from-scratch asset. | local | passed (test) |
| `studio-drafts-persist`: A new resource-backed Studio asset can be saved without publication, survives host restart, remains workspace-isolated, and retains source bytes only in bounded immutable artifact storage. | local | passed (test) |
| `saved-reopens-exact-draft`: Saved lists unpublished assets and opens the selected exact draft with all semantic and backing-resource content restored in Studio. | local | passed (test) |
| `studio-transports-aligned`: Server API and desktop IPC/preload operations enforce the same validation, workspace authorization, optimistic revision, sanitized failure, and bounded resource semantics. | local | passed (test) |
| `studio-review-publish-safe`: Review materializes an immutable source snapshot and publication creates a distinct definition plus implementation draft without build, activation, deployment, or execution. | local | passed (test) |
| `asset-tabs-consolidated`: Create is absent, Drafts is labeled Saved, Customizations remains dedicated to derived copies, and cross-tab handoff never splits editing across multiple tabs. | local | passed (test) |

### Verification

- Run focused contract, application, persistence, artifact, API, IPC, preload, client, shared-section, Studio, Saved-navigation, restart, workspace-isolation, and negative security tests while each chunk is active.
- After every Increment 5 chunk passes focused checks, run desktop TypeScript/package validation, server and thin-client builds, docs:check, architecture:check, agent-support:check, git diff validation, and npm test once.

### Rollback

Keep legacy authored-draft reads compatible and all new records readable; disable new Studio mutation capabilities and restore the prior tabs without deleting saved drafts, artifacts, snapshots, or published definitions.

### Excluded

- Executing authored code in the product renderer, Electron main process, or API server
- Automatic dependency installation, build, activation, deployment, or publication
- Public marketplace or registry behavior
- Cross-workspace collaborative editing

## Increment 6: End-to-end production qualification and hardening

- Id: `production-qualification`
- Status: `implemented-pending-qualification`
- Dependencies: `unified-asset-studio-saved`

Prove the complete Assets and Systems experience, layered customization, and unified resource-backed Studio behavior across supported hosts, representative bases and new assets, restart persistence, failure and security modes, responsive layouts, accessibility expectations, and canonical documentation.

### Work packages

- **Representative end-to-end scenarios** (`scenario-tests`): Tests cover default or system and admitted imported customization plus new Studio asset save, reopen, review, publication, browse visibility, restart persistence, and original immutability on desktop and server paths.
- **Failure and security qualification** (`failure-security`): Cross-workspace access, stale revisions or bases, unsafe paths or content, oversized files, revoked or unavailable package truth, interrupted persistence, and unavailable Studio adapters fail closed with recoverable safe UI states.
- **Accessibility and responsive qualification** (`accessibility-responsive`): Keyboard, focus, modal stacking, tab semantics, screen-reader naming and status, 400-percent zoom and reflow, contrast, and narrow-layout checks are recorded for desktop and thin client.
- **Documentation and release evidence** (`documentation-release`): Canonical architecture, security, package authoring, UI guidance, context packs, READMEs, support qualification, and durable roadmap and report state match implemented behavior and limitations.

### Deliverables

- End-to-end and negative regression coverage
- Desktop and thin-client build and package evidence
- Accessibility and responsive review evidence
- Updated canonical docs, context, READMEs, and support qualification
- Final implementation report with commands, results, risks, and limitations
